facts.fact: ZIMRA states that TaRMS Releases 1 and 2 (registration, returns, payments, refunds, revenue and taxpayer accounting, debt management) are already implemented in production, with first modules live 12 October 2023 and Release 3 due 1 October 2024.
The African Development Bank states Zimbabwe completed deployment of a new online Tax and Revenue Management System, formally launched in Harare on 18 August 2025 after phased rollout from 2023.
The African Development Bank, citing ZIMRA, states revenue from new taxpayers rose 238% in 2024, the first full year after rollout of TaRMS began, compared with 2023.

note: Notice announces Release 3 modules to roll out on 1 October 2024 (future at issue); it does not state the system is in use.

facts.fact: The e-Governance Academy states it completed a customised government enterprise architecture framework, plan and roadmap for Zimbabwe between September 2023 and September 2024, with over 40 MDAs taking part, and that the model is now in place.

note: Page undated; project end September 2024 used as the date.

facts.fact: The Public Service Commission states the legacy SPACE payroll system, operating since 1994, still runs government payroll while GovPay is tested in parallel, with full GovPay launch targeted for the first or second quarter of 2026.

facts.fact: ZIMRA's Public Notice 63 of 2025 (issued 14 November 2025) states that the Tax and Revenue Management System (TaRMS) already handles VAT return submission through a Tax Returns Management Module and taxpayer Self-Service Portal, with an upgrade and FDMS integration taking effect on 1 December 2025.

The Auditor-General's report on the 2023 accounts describes the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) as an Enterprise Resource Planning platform used by Ministries and Commissions to process financial transactions, and audits its controls; Treasury Instructions 2019 require all payments to go through it.

The Auditor-General reports that in 2023 Treasury paid ZWL$34 billion (US$277 million) directly to suppliers outside the PFMS, and that some Fund Accounts used manual systems instead, so PFMS coverage was incomplete.

facts.fact: ZIMRA Public Notice 75 of 2024 says taxpayers file VAT, PAYE, income, withholding and presumptive tax returns online in its Tax Revenue Management System (TaRMS), which charges penalties automatically and issues tax clearance certificates automatically.

ZIMRA says TaRMS, replacing SAP TRM for domestic taxes, launched its Return Management, Payments Management, Taxpayer Accounting and Debt Management modules on 6 December 2023, with Release 2 live from 29 February 2024.
ZIMRA says TaRMS replaced SAP TRM as the domestic taxes system, going live in phases from 12 October 2023.

facts.fact: ZIMRA Public Notice 78 of 2024 says TaRMS Release 3 went live on 1 October 2024 and marks the full implementation of the Tax and Revenue Management System.
ZIMRA Public Notice 78 of 2024 says the final phase of TaRMS, Release 3 with four modules, went live on 1 October 2024.

facts.fact: ZIMRA commissioned TaRMS on 18 August 2025, the tax administration and revenue system that replaced its SAP-based legacy setup and is in use for filing, payments and refunds.
ZIMRA's release schedule shows TaRMS Release 1 (user management, TIN registration, return filing, payments) went live in December 2023, replacing the legacy SAP system.
